writtenBefore: any 2023 data was fetched or looked at; committed before the fetch so git history shows the order
question: Does pulling every ranked team down by its number of losses (so close calls break toward the better record) beat the live model on a season it wasn't tuned on?
why: The Nov 6 cohort analysis (2024-2026, descriptive) found voters sort by loss count more than the live model does: about 40% of the live model's wrong pairs had voters putting the fewer-loss team on top, more than half of them in weeks where the more-loss team didn't lose, and the model leaves a top-10 team's 2nd loss too high (5.3 fewer-loss teams still below it vs 3.1 real). A per-game loss term can't see a team's record in a week it wins or has a bye; this term applies every week. The user's starting idea was narrower (a 3rd loss drops a team below the 2-loss teams), so that version is tested too.

holdout.construction: identical to experiments 1-2: scripts/fetch-pickem-history.mjs (CFBD /rankings, /games, /lines, regular season), scripts/lib/pickem-history.mjs (same Elo stand-ins, quality-win rule, and alignment check); losses per team counted from that season's regular-season finals through each poll week's games

check.transitions: poll weeks 1-9 (week 3 live snapshot, the rest rebuilt from git), each against the next AP poll from data/current.json; losses from current.json's game logs

context.use: 2024 and 2025 together are where the values were fit (scripts/fit-loss-pull.mjs); 2025 is reported for reference, not evidence

metric: weighted pairwise order errors, exactly as experiments 1-2 (transitions out of poll weeks 1-2 weigh 0.5, later 1.0; exits tied just below #25; entrants not scored)

LP.source: 2024+2025, one-standard-error rule over lossCountPull [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4] on LIVE; best 1 (380.5 vs 424 weighted errors), reported 0.75 (386). Refitting lossScale with the pull in place kept 2.5.

L3.source: the narrower 3rd-loss version: 2024+2025, same rule over lossPullFrom3 [0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8] on LIVE; best and reported 1 (410 vs 424)

chain.asks: does a per-loss pull on every team beat the live model on a new season?
if the broad pull failed, does the narrow 3rd-loss pull pass?

chain.label: 3rd-loss extra 1
chain.asks: does an extra 3rd-loss pull add anything on top of LP? (2024+2025 said no: 386 at 0 and at 1)

passRule: a step's candidate replaces the current model only if, on 2023: weighted errors fall (delta > 0); the 5th percentile of the summed improvement over 10,000 bootstrap resamples of 2023 transitions (seed 20260923) is > 0; neither half of the season (poll weeks 1-8, 9+) gets worse; and the improvement stays > 0 after removing every pair involving any single team
checkGuard: the final model's weighted errors on 2026 weeks 1-9 must not exceed LIVE's; if they do, fall back through the adopted models to the last one that passes
outcome: the chain's final model is the recommendation; nothing ships to the live page without the user's go-ahead; every model's numbers on 2023, 2026 and 2025 are reported either way
